newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina cancels international customs meeting.
newsitem.headline: Argentina cancels international customs meeting.

text.p: Argentina has canceled a meeting of customs directors from Latin America, Spain and Portugal slated to open Monday, citing the restructuring of its own customs service, a spokesman announced.
Organizers of the 17th International Meeting of Customs Directors from Latin America, Spain and Portugal will have to decide on another date and venue, the Argentine customs spokesman said.
The weeklong meeting was to take place in the central city of Carlos Paz. Discussions were expected to focus on how to improve the flow of goods between member countries.

The spokesman said Carlos Silvani, the newly appointed head of the Argentine service -- which has been jolted by a series of corruption and smuggling scandals -- decided it was not the right time for the country to host the meeting.

The customs service is being merged with the tax collection agency DGI in an effort to stop contraband, which cost the government $3.0 billion in uncollected tariffs in the past four years, according to official estimates.
